definition_en: to make someone feel less confident, or to try to stop someone from doing something
core_image: 一只手刚抬起来要往前，另一只手从旁边轻轻把它按下去
scene: 报名表还摊在桌上，笔尖停在半空。One failed attempt should not discourage you.
sceneCN: 这里 discourage 指「使气馁」（第 1 个义项：让人失去信心）；句意是一次失败不该让你泄气。

senses.title: To drain the will to try
senses.definition: to make someone feel less confident or less hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 让人失去信心或希望
senses.example: One bad grade should not discourage you.
senses.exampleCN: 一次糟糕的成绩不该让你气馁。
senses.why: Courage is a supply, and a few cold words can empty it.
senses.whyCN: 勇气像一份存量，几句冷话就能把它掏空。

senses.title: To talk someone out of an act
senses.definition: to try to stop someone from doing something by pointing at doubt or difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 用怀疑或困难让对方打消做某事的念头
senses.example: The teacher discouraged us from copying answers.
senses.exampleCN: 老师劝我们不要抄答案。
senses.why: A hand raised to stop is gentler than a door slammed shut.
senses.whyCN: 抬手拦住，比摔门关上要温和。

intro.en: Discourage joins dis-, meaning away, to the Latin cor, the heart, so the word pictures courage being taken out of the chest.
intro.cn: discourage 由表示「拿走」的 dis- 与拉丁语的心 cor 组成，画面是把勇气从胸口取走。

items.en: Cor, cordis meant the heart, and Romans placed courage there.
items.cn: cor 指心，罗马人把勇气安放在心里。

items.en: Descoragier meant to strip away heart or spirit.
items.cn: 古法语 descoragier 指把心气剥掉。

items.en: English borrowed it to mean deprive of courage.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示使失去勇气。

items.en: The sense widened to holding someone back from an act.
items.cn: 词义扩大，也指拦住别人不让做某事。

items.en: Today it covers both a lost heart and a friendly warning.
items.cn: 今天它既指心里泄气，也指好言拦阻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the courage stem, while the meaning group gathers words for warning someone off.
note.cn: 形近组共享 courage 这一段，近义组则是几个表示劝退或泄气的词。

entries.definition: the strength to face fear
to give someone hope or support
the feeling of lost hope
to make someone decide not to act
to take away hope or spirit
to persuade someone not to do something

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a hand pressing another hand down.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守住一幅画面：一只手把另一只手按下去。

normal.en: Dis- plus courage means courage taken out.
normal.cn: dis 加 courage，就是把勇气拿走。

normal.en: A coach who lists only failures discourages the whole team.
normal.cn: 教练只数落失败，整支队伍都会泄气。

normal.en: One cold comment can discourage a new learner.
normal.cn: 一句冷话就能让新学的人泄气。

normal.en: Friends discourage you from quitting by naming the risk.
normal.cn: 朋友点出风险，劝你别辞职。

normal.en: Discouraged parents stop asking the school for changes.
normal.cn: 心灰意冷的家长不再向学校提要求。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing another hand gently down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手轻轻把另一只手按下去。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon losing air until it lies flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球漏气，最后瘪在地上。

abstract.en: Picture a voice at the door saying not yet.
abstract.cn: 想象门口有个声音说，再等等。

examples.en: Do not let one bad review discourage you.
examples.cn: 别让一条差评让你泄气。

examples.en: The rain discouraged most of the visitors.
examples.cn: 这场雨让大多数游客打消了念头。

examples.en: She was discouraged by the long waiting list.
examples.cn: 长长的等候名单让她泄了气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discourage 记成「抽走勇气」：dis 是拿走，courage 是勇气，勇气被拿走，人就泄气，也会劝人别做。

root: 来自古法语 descoragier，词根是拉丁语 cor（心），加前缀 dis- 表示拿走，本义是把心气抽走。英语里先指使人失去勇气，后也指用言语劝人放弃某件事。

sensesIntro.en: From a heart that loses its nerve, to a friend who talks you out of the plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一颗失去底气的心，到一位劝你放弃计划的朋友。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed gently down on another hand as it starts to rise.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手刚刚抬起，另一只手轻轻把它按下去。

branches.en: The first sense is the inward loss of nerve.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是心里那点底气被抽走。

branches.en: The second sense turns that loss into advice for someone else.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这种泄气变成对别人的劝告。

branches.en: Both senses remove the will before the act begins.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在行动开始前先拿走意愿。

branches.en: Both can be caused by a single sentence from a stranger.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能被陌生人的一句话造成。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs another person in front of you.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要眼前另有一个人才成立。

intro.en: Discourage gathers the courage family, with Latin cor, the heart, at its centre.
intro.cn: discourage 聚起 courage 一族，中心是拉丁语里表示心的 cor。

latinIntro.en: Latin cor, heart, gives cord- and courage; dis- and en- push the same stem in opposite directions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cor（心）给出 cord 与 courage，前缀 dis- 与 en- 把同一词干推向相反方向。

items.meaning: the heart as the seat of bravery
items.example: It takes courage to speak first.
Her note encouraged the whole class.
He sounded discouraged on the phone.
items.exampleCN: 他在电话里听起来很泄气。

items.meaning: in a way that kills hope
items.example: She spoke discouragingly of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她谈起这个计划时很泄气。

definition_en: to find something or learn a fact for the first time
core_image: 草丛被拨开，地上露出一只从没被记录的脚印
scene: 雨后的泥地很软，他蹲下去看那串新鲜的痕迹。She discovered a hidden path behind the house.
sceneCN: 这里 discover 指「发现」（第 1 个义项：找到原本存在却不为人知的东西）；句意是她发现屋后有一条隐蔽的小路。

collocations.phrase: discover that the door was open

senses.title: To come upon what was hidden
senses.definition: to find something that existed before but was not known
senses.definitionCN: 找到原本存在却不为人知的东西
senses.example: Scientists discovered a new kind of frog.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家发现了一种新的青蛙。
senses.why: A page turns, and a room that was always there appears.
senses.whyCN: 翻过一页，一间一直都在的屋子忽然出现。

senses.title: To learn a fact
senses.definition: to learn or realize something you did not know before
senses.definitionCN: 得知或意识到自己原先不知道的事
senses.example: I discovered that the shop closes at six.
senses.exampleCN: 我发觉那家店六点关门。
senses.why: The world does not change; only your picture of it does.
senses.whyCN: 世界没变，变的是你心里那张图。

intro.en: Discover is Latin dis-, undoing, plus cooperire, to cover: to take the cover off something.
intro.cn: discover 是拉丁语 dis-（去掉）加 cooperire（覆盖），本义是把盖子揭开。

items.en: Cooperire meant to cover something completely.
items.cn: cooperire 指把东西完全盖住。

items.en: Dis- undid that cover, so the thing stood bare.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把覆盖去掉，东西就露了出来。

items.en: Descovrir meant to uncover or lay bare.
items.cn: 古法语 descovrir 指揭开覆盖、露出本来面目。

items.en: English took it as to reveal or find out.
items.cn: 英语借入时表示揭露或查明。

items.en: The word now covers a lucky find and a slow research.
items.cn: 今天它既指偶然碰上，也指长期研究所得。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the cover stem, and the meaning group lists other ways of finding.
note.cn: 形近组保留 cover 这段词干，近义组列出别的表示找到的词。

entries.definition: to put something over another thing
to remove a cover or bring to light
the act or result of finding
to come upon something by chance or search
to notice something hidden or faint
to see something suddenly

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lifted cover and end with a fact that fits into place.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从揭开的盖子开始，落到终于对上位置的一件事。

normal.en: Dis- plus cover: take the cover off.
normal.cn: dis 加 cover，就是把盖子揭开。

normal.en: A child discovers a beetle under a stone.
normal.cn: 孩子在石头下面发现一只甲虫。

normal.en: You discover the truth when two stories stop matching.
normal.cn: 两个说法对不上时，你就发现了真相。

normal.en: A discovered path shortens the walk home.
normal.cn: 发现的小路让回家的路变短。

normal.en: Science discovers slowly, one careful step at a time.
normal.cn: 科学发现很慢，一次只走一小步。

abstract.en: Picture a cloth pulled back from a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布从桌面被拉开。

abstract.en: Picture a torch beam finding a door in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象手电的光在黑暗里找到一扇门。

abstract.en: Picture a blank line on a map filled with a name.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一段空白被填上名字。

examples.en: She discovered a small door behind the shelf.
examples.cn: 她发现书架后面有一扇小门。

examples.en: We discovered that the train had already left.
examples.cn: 我们发觉火车已经开走了。

examples.en: The team discovered a new cave last summer.
examples.cn: 去年夏天那支队伍发现了一个新洞穴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discover 记成「揭开盖子」：dis 是去掉，cover 是盖子，盖子一揭，藏着的东西就露出来。

root: 源自拉丁语 cooperire（覆盖）加否定前缀 dis-，经古法语 descovrir 进入英语，本义是揭开覆盖之物。后来从「露出」引申为「找到原本就在那里、只是没人知道的东西」，也指得知一件事实。

sensesIntro.en: From lifting a cover off something hidden to learning a plain fact about the world.
sensesIntro.cn: 从揭开藏物上的覆盖，到得知世上的一件普通事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth lifted, and something that was always there stands revealed.
core.cn: 核心意象：布被掀开，一直都在的东西露了出来。

branches.en: The first sense is the moment a hidden thing shows itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是藏物露出来的那一刻。

branches.en: The second sense moves the find inside the mind, as knowledge.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把发现搬进心里，变成知识。

branches.en: Both senses begin with something unknown and end with it known.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从不知道开始，到知道为止。

branches.en: Both can happen by accident or by long search.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能是偶然，也可能是长久的寻找。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be a small everyday fact.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项可以是一件日常小事。

intro.en: Discover sits in the cover family, where dis-, un- and re- each change what the cover does.
intro.cn: discover 属于 cover 一族，前缀 dis-、un-、re- 改变的都是盖子被怎样处理。

latinIntro.en: Latin cooperire, to cover, gives the stem cover-, which carries dis-, un- and re- in turn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cooperire（覆盖）给出词干 cover，依次接上 dis-、un- 与 re-。

items.example: They discovered a cave behind the falls.
items.exampleCN: 他们发现瀑布后面有个洞。

items.meaning: the act or result of finding

items.example: The discoverer was a young doctor.
items.exampleCN: 发现者是一位年轻医生。
这个错误很容易被发现。

items.example: An undiscovered island remains on the chart.
items.exampleCN: 海图上还有一座未被发现的岛。
他重新找到了一位老朋友。

items.example: An undercover officer watched the door.
items.exampleCN: 一名便衣警员盯着那扇门。

definition_en: the act of finding something for the first time, or the thing that is found
core_image: 旧地图上一块空白刚被红笔圈出一个新名字
scene: 灯光照着那张旧地图，红笔的圆圈还没干。The discovery of the tunnel changed the whole plan.
sceneCN: 这里 discovery 指「发现」（第 1 个义项：找到不为人知的事物的行为）；句意是那条隧道的发现改变了整个计划。

collocations.zh: 物理学上的一项新发现

senses.title: The act of finding
senses.definition: the act or process of finding something not known before
senses.definitionCN: 找到原先不为人知之物的行为或过程
senses.example: The discovery of the letter solved the mystery.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信的发现解开了谜团。
senses.why: Someone walks past the same wall for years, then one day stops.
senses.whyCN: 同一堵墙走过多年，终于有一天停了下来。

senses.title: The thing that is found
senses.definition: a thing, place or fact that has been found for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 第一次被找到的东西、地点或事实
senses.example: The old coin turned out to be an important discovery.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚旧硬币后来成了重要发现。
senses.why: A find is small enough to hold, yet it redraws the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 一件发现小得可以捧在手里，却把整片领域重画。

intro.en: Discovery is discover plus -y; the stem goes back to Latin dis- and cooperire, to uncover.
intro.cn: discovery 是 discover 加名词后缀 -y；词干可追到拉丁语 dis- 与 cooperire（揭开覆盖）。

items.en: Cooperire meant to cover, and dis- meant the opposite.
items.cn: cooperire 指覆盖，dis- 表示相反的动作。

items.en: Descovrir, to uncover, entered French from that Latin pair.
items.cn: descovrir 由这对拉丁成分进入法语，意为揭开。

items.en: The verb discover came first, meaning to reveal.
items.cn: 先有动词 discover，表示揭露。

items.en: The noun discovery named the act and later the thing found.
items.cn: 名词 discovery 先指行为，后也指找到的东西。

items.en: Science gave it the weight of a formal result.
items.cn: 科学语境让它带上了正式成果的分量。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the discover stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of finds.
note.cn: 形近组建在 discover 词干上，近义组列出别的所得。

entries.definition: to find something not known before
entries.definitionCN: 找到原先不为人知的东西

entries.definition: a person who finds something first
to remove a cover or reveal
a result or fact that has been found
a sudden important advance
the act of noticing something hidden

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a circle drawn on a blank map and end with a field redrawn.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从空白图上画出的一个圈开始，落到一片被重画的领域。

normal.en: Discovery is discover with -y, the act made into a thing.
normal.cn: discovery 是 discover 加 -y，把行为变成了东西。

normal.en: A discovery begins where a question is left open.
normal.cn: 发现始于一个没被合上的问题。

normal.en: The discovery of a single bone can rebuild a whole animal.
normal.cn: 一根骨头的发现能重建整只动物。

normal.en: Good notes turn a lucky discovery into knowledge.
normal.cn: 好笔记把偶然的发现变成知识。

normal.en: Every discovery makes the old map wrong somewhere.
normal.cn: 每一次发现都让旧地图有一处不再正确。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn in red on a blank map.
abstract.cn: 想象空白地图上画出一个红圈。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held low over wet ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯低低照着湿地面。

abstract.en: Picture a name being written under a photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象照片底下写上一个名字。

examples.en: The discovery of the tunnel changed the whole plan.
examples.cn: 那条隧道的发现改变了整个计划。

examples.en: She made an important discovery in the archive.
examples.cn: 她在档案里有一项重要发现。

examples.en: Recent discoveries have changed the story of the city.
examples.cn: 近来的发现改变了这座城的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discovery 记成「揭开盖子看见的东西」：dis 去掉，cover 盖子，-y 变名词，揭盖之后所见就是发现。

root: 由动词 discover 加名词后缀 -y 构成；discover 源自拉丁语 cooperire（覆盖）加 dis-，经古法语 descovrir 进入英语，本义是揭开覆盖。因此 discovery 既指揭开的过程，也指被揭出来的东西。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of lifting a cover to the object that lies underneath.
sensesIntro.cn: 从揭开覆盖的动作，到覆盖底下那件东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red circle closing around a name that was not on the map before.
core.cn: 核心意象：红笔圈住一个从前不在图上的名字。

branches.en: The first sense is the work and the moment of finding.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是寻找的过程与找到的那一刻。

branches.en: The second sense is the object or fact that comes out of it.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是从中出来的物件或事实。

branches.en: An act and its object share one name in English.
branches.cn: 在英语里，行为与结果共用一个名字。

branches.en: Both senses change what people thought they knew.
branches.cn: 两个义项都改变人们原以为知道的东西。

branches.en: Only the second sense can sit in a museum case.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能放进博物馆的展柜。

intro.en: Discovery sits at the noun end of the cover family: discover, discoverer, discoverable.
intro.cn: discovery 站在 cover 一族的名词一端，同族还有 discover、discoverer 与 discoverable。

latinIntro.en: Latin cooperire, to cover, yields cover and discover, and the suffix -y makes the finding a thing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cooperire（覆盖）给出 cover 与 discover，后缀 -y 再把找到这件事变成东西。

items.meaning: the act or result of finding
items.example: The discovery was kept secret for a year.
items.exampleCN: 这一发现被保密了一年。

items.example: The discoverer wrote a short report.
items.exampleCN: 发现者写了一份简短报告。

items.example: The pattern is discoverable in the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个规律在数据里可以被发现。

items.meaning: a finding again of something old
items.example: The rediscovery of the recipe pleased cooks.
items.exampleCN: 这道菜谱的重新发现让厨师们高兴。

items.example: An undiscovered room lay above the hall.
items.exampleCN: 大厅上方有一间未被发现的房间。

definition_en: unfair treatment of a group of people, or the ability to see fine differences
core_image: 两张几乎一样的简历被推向桌子两边，一边的椅子却更高
scene: 两叠简历内容几乎一样，却被推向了不同的方向。She spoke out against discrimination in hiring.
sceneCN: 这里 discrimination 指「歧视」（第 1 个义项：因群体身份而受的不公平对待）；句意是她公开反对招聘中的歧视。

senses.title: Unfair treatment of a group
senses.definition: the unfair treatment of people because of their group, age or sex
senses.definitionCN: 因所属群体、年龄或性别而受到的不公平对待
senses.example: The law forbids discrimination at work.
senses.exampleCN: 法律禁止职场歧视。
senses.why: A line is drawn first, and then one side is given less.
senses.whyCN: 先画一道线，然后让一边少拿。

senses.title: The power to tell things apart
senses.definition: the ability to see small differences between things
senses.definitionCN: 看出事物之间细微差别的能力
senses.example: Good tea needs a fine discrimination of smell.
senses.exampleCN: 懂好茶需要精细的嗅觉辨别力。
senses.why: The same sharp eye that separates can also sort people unfairly.
senses.whyCN: 能分辨的锐利眼光，也可能被用来不公平地分流人群。

intro.en: Discrimination comes from Latin discriminare, to divide or separate, from discrimen, a dividing line.
intro.cn: discrimination 来自拉丁语 discriminare（分开、区分），其根 discrimen 指分界线。

items.en: Discrimen meant a line that separates two things.
items.cn: discrimen 指把两样东西分开的界线。

items.en: Discriminare meant to divide or to distinguish.
items.cn: discriminare 指划分或加以区别。

items.en: English used it for the act of telling differences.
items.cn: 英语借入后指辨别差异的行为。

items.en: The sense of unfair treatment by group grew in law and politics.
items.cn: 按群体不公平对待这一义项在法律与政治中长出来。

items.en: Both the sharp eye and the closed door keep the same word.
items.cn: 敏锐的眼光与关上的门，共用这一个词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the discrimin- stem, and the meaning group names unfair attitudes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 discrimin- 词干，近义组列出几种不公平的态度。

entries.definition: to see a difference or to treat unfairly
entries.definitionCN: 分辨差异或加以不公平对待

entries.definition: able to judge fine differences
done without any choice or care
a leaning that makes judgement unfair
an opinion formed before the facts
entries.definitionCN: 未看事实就形成的看法

entries.definition: the quality of not being just

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a chalk line and end with a hand that can weigh two shades.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道粉笔线开始，落到一只能掂量两种色差的手。

normal.en: Discrimin- means to separate; -ion makes it a practice.
normal.cn: discrimin- 是分开，-ion 把它变成一种做法。

normal.en: A line drawn around a group soon becomes a wall.
normal.cn: 围着某个群体画下的线，很快会变成墙。

normal.en: The same word praises a fine palate and blames a closed door.
normal.cn: 同一个词既夸精细的品味，也指责关上的门。

normal.en: Discrimination at work can hide inside a polite rule.
normal.cn: 职场歧视能藏在一条规定里。

normal.en: A discriminating reader notices the missing sentence.
normal.cn: 有辨别力的读者看得出少掉的那一句。

abstract.en: Picture one line of chalk across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面上划过一道粉笔线。

abstract.en: Picture two identical files placed at different heights.
abstract.cn: 想象两份一样的档案被放在不同高度。

abstract.en: Picture an eye that can weigh two almost equal colours.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼能掂量两种几乎相同的颜色。

examples.en: The company was sued for discrimination.
examples.cn: 这家公司因歧视被起诉。

examples.en: She has a fine discrimination of taste and smell.
examples.cn: 她对味道与气味有精细的辨别力。

examples.en: Age discrimination is hard to prove.
examples.cn: 年龄歧视很难证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discrimination 记成「划线分开」：discrimin- 是划分，-ion 是行为；把人按群体划开并少给，就是歧视；把事物细细划开，就是辨别力。

root: 源自拉丁语 discrimen（分界线）与 discriminare（划分、区别），进入英语后先指辨别差异，十九世纪起在法律与政治语境里指按群体给予不公平对待，于是同一个词兼有「辨别力」与「歧视」两面。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of drawing a line between things, to the unfair line drawn around people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从在事物之间划线，到围着人群划出的一条不公平的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chalk line across a table, with one side quietly given less.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌面上一道粉笔线，一边悄悄少拿了东西。

chain: THE LINE HARDENS INTO A WALL

branches.en: The first sense is the wall built around a group.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是围着某个群体砌起的墙。

branches.en: The second sense is the eye that can weigh fine shades.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是能掂量细微差别的眼睛。

branches.en: Both start from the same act of separating.
branches.cn: 两个义项都始于同一个分开的动作。

branches.en: Both need a line before anything can be sorted.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有线，才能分拣。

branches.en: Only the second sense is a skill worth training.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项是值得训练的本事。

intro.en: Discrimination belongs to the Latin discrimin- family, where separating and sorting share one root.
intro.cn: discrimination 属于拉丁语 discrimin- 一族，区分与分拣共用同一个根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin discrimen, a dividing line, gives discriminare and then discrimination in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discrimen（分界线）给出 discriminare，再进入英语成为 discrimination。

items.meaning: the act of separating or treating unfairly

items.example: The test discriminates between two groups.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试把两组人区分开。
这条规定被称为歧视性的。
她有一双有辨别力的耳朵。
这张网不加区分地捕鱼。

items.meaning: the practice of not treating people unfairly
a thing that separates one from another
items.example: The device is a simple discriminator.
items.exampleCN: 这个装置是个简单的鉴别器。

definition_en: to talk about something with others, or to examine a subject in speech or writing
core_image: 几个人围着一张桌子，手指在纸上来回点
scene: 桌上摊着一张计划表，几根手指同时点向同一行。We need to discuss the budget before Friday.
sceneCN: 这里 discuss 指「讨论」（第 1 个义项：与他人交换看法）；句意是我们得在周五前讨论预算。

senses.title: To exchange views on a subject
senses.definition: to talk about a subject with other people and hear different views
senses.definitionCN: 与他人谈论某个话题并听取不同看法
senses.example: We discussed the plan over lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃午饭时讨论了那个计划。
senses.why: Two heads turn the same fact until a new side shows.
senses.whyCN: 两个脑袋把一个事实翻来转去，转出新的侧面。

senses.title: To examine a subject in writing
senses.definition: to examine a subject in speech or writing in an organized way
senses.definitionCN: 以有条理的方式口头或书面探讨某个主题
senses.example: The report discusses three causes of the failure.
senses.exampleCN: 报告论述了失败的三个原因。
senses.why: A page can hold a conversation that nobody is having aloud.
senses.whyCN: 一页纸能装下一场没人出声的对话。

intro.en: Discuss comes from Latin discutere, to strike apart, built from dis- and quatere, to shake.
intro.cn: discuss 来自拉丁语 discutere（打散、击碎），由 dis- 与 quatere（摇、击）组成。

items.en: Quatere meant to shake or strike.
items.cn: quatere 指摇动或击打。

items.en: Discutere meant to strike apart and so to examine closely.
items.cn: discutere 指打散，因而引申为细查。

items.en: English took it as to examine or argue a case.
items.cn: 英语借入时表示审查或争辩一个案子。

items.en: The sense settled into talking a matter over.
items.cn: 词义固定为把事情谈开。

items.en: Writing can discuss a subject without any voice at all.
items.cn: 书面文字也能论述主题，不必有声音。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the discuss stem, and the meaning group gathers other forms of talk.
note.cn: 形近组来自 discuss 词干，近义组聚起别的谈话形式。

entries.definition: a conversation about a subject
a person who takes part in a discussion
talked about by many people
a formal argument with two sides
to give reasons for or against something
entries.definitionCN: 为赞成或反对给出理由

entries.definition: to talk something over with others

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with fingers on one line and end with a page that keeps the talk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从手指点在同一行开始，落到一页留住谈话的纸。

normal.en: Dis- plus cuss: the matter is struck apart for a look.
normal.cn: dis 加 cuss，就是把事情打散来看。

normal.en: Two engineers discuss a crack until the cause is clear.
normal.cn: 两个工程师讨论一道裂纹，直到原因清楚。

normal.en: Families discuss money best at a table, not at a door.
normal.cn: 一家人谈钱，最好在桌边，不在门口。

normal.en: The report discusses what the meeting only hinted at.
normal.cn: 报告论述了会上只隐约提到的部分。

normal.en: A discussed problem is half solved.
normal.cn: 被讨论过的问题，已经解决了一半。

abstract.en: Picture four fingers tapping the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象四根手指点在同一行上。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet turned round and round.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸被转来转去。

abstract.en: Picture a pen drawing a line under one word.
abstract.cn: 想象笔在一个词底下画了一道。

examples.en: We need to discuss the budget before Friday.
examples.cn: 我们得在周五前讨论预算。

examples.en: The article discusses three reasons for the change.
examples.cn: 这篇文章论述了这一变化的三个原因。

examples.en: They discussed the matter for two hours.
examples.cn: 他们商量这件事商量了两个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discuss 记成「把话打散」：dis 是分开，cuss 与击打同源；把一件事敲碎摊开，大家一块看，就是讨论。

root: 源自拉丁语 discutere（打散、细查），由 dis-（分开）与 quatere（摇、击）构成，本义是把东西击碎摊开来看。进入英语后先指审查辩论，后来固定为「讨论」，再引申出书面上的「论述」。

sensesIntro.en: From striking a matter apart to see its pieces, to the calm page that sets them in order.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把一件事打散看清各块，到把各块摆整齐的那页文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several fingers tapping the same line on one sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：几根手指同时点在同一张纸的同一行上。

branches.en: The first sense is the round of voices at the table.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是桌边一轮又一轮的声音。

branches.en: The second sense lets the page do the talking later.
branches.cn: 第二个义项让纸页在事后替人说话。

branches.en: Both take a subject apart before putting it together.
branches.cn: 两个义项都先拆开话题，再把它拼上。

branches.en: Both can be long, slow and unfinished.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能漫长、缓慢、没有结论。

branches.en: Only the second sense appears in print.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项会出现在印刷品里。

intro.en: Discuss keeps the Latin stem cuss-, to strike, which also hides inside percussion.
intro.cn: discuss 保留拉丁词干 cuss-（击打），这个词干也藏在 percussion 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin quatere, to shake, becomes -cuss- in discuss and discussus in the past participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quatere（摇动）在 discuss 中变成 cuss-，过去分词是 discussus。

items.example: They discussed the map at length.
items.exampleCN: 他们详细讨论了那张地图。

items.meaning: a conversation that examines a subject
one who takes part in a discussion
in the act of talking over
a striking through, as on a drum
items.exampleCN: 打击乐为这首曲子开场。

definition_en: a conversation in which people share views on a subject, or a written treatment of it
core_image: 一张写满字的纸被推到桌子中间，几个人轮流指着其中一行
scene: 纸页被推到桌子中间，几个人轮流指着上面的一行。The discussion lasted until the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里 discussion 指「讨论」（第 1 个义项：交换看法的谈话）；句意是讨论一直持续到熄灯。

senses.title: A conversation of shared views
senses.definition: a conversation in which people exchange views on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 人们就某个话题交换看法的谈话
senses.example: The discussion lasted until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论一直持续到半夜。
senses.why: A table of voices is cheaper than a table of mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 一桌人的声音，比一桌错误便宜。

senses.title: A written treatment of a subject
senses.definition: a section of writing that examines a subject in detail
senses.definitionCN: 详细探讨某一主题的书面部分
senses.example: The final chapter is a discussion of risk.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一章是对风险的论述。
senses.why: The talk leaves the room and becomes a page.
senses.whyCN: 谈话离开屋子，变成一页纸。

intro.en: Discussion is discuss plus -ion, from Latin discutere, to strike apart and examine.
intro.cn: discussion 是 discuss 加 -ion，源自拉丁语 discutere（打散、细查）。

items.en: Discutere meant to shake a thing apart.
items.cn: discutere 指把东西摇散。

items.en: The participle discussus described a thing broken open.
items.cn: 过去分词 discussus 形容被打开的东西。

items.en: The noun first named a formal examination of a case.
items.cn: 这个名词最早指对案子的正式审查。

items.en: It came to mean a talk among several people.
items.cn: 后来指几个人之间的谈话。

items.en: Essays now carry discussion as a named section.
items.cn: 如今文章里也用 discussion 作章节名。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the discuss stem, and the meaning group lists other kinds of exchange.
note.cn: 形近组保留 discuss 词干，近义组列出别的交流方式。

entries.definition: to talk a subject over
a person who joins a discussion
talked about by other people
a formal exchange of opposing views
an informal talk between people
a talk that aims at understanding
entries.definitionCN: 以求理解为目的的对话

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a sheet pushed to the middle and end with a chapter that keeps it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从推到桌中的一张纸开始，落到把它留下的一章。

normal.en: Discussion is discuss plus -ion, the talk turned into a noun.
normal.cn: discussion 是 discuss 加 -ion，把谈话变成名词。

normal.en: A group discussion needs one quiet listener to work.
normal.cn: 小组讨论需要一个安静的听众才成。

normal.en: Under discussion means the answer is still moving.
normal.cn: 在讨论中，意思是答案还在动。

normal.en: A panel discussion puts five voices in one row.
normal.cn: 专家讨论把五个声音排成一排。

normal.en: The discussion section of a paper admits what is still unknown.
normal.cn: 论文的论述部分会承认还未知的事。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet sliding to the centre of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸滑到桌子中央。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to take the next turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，准备接下一轮。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp still on after everyone has agreed.
abstract.cn: 想象大家说定之后，灯还亮着。

examples.en: The discussion lasted until the lights went out.
examples.cn: 讨论一直持续到熄灯。

examples.en: We had a long discussion about the new rules.
examples.cn: 我们就新规定进行了长时间的讨论。

examples.en: Her paper ends with a discussion of memory.
examples.cn: 她的论文以一节关于记忆的论述收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discussion 记成「打散之后的谈」：discuss 是把事敲开来看，加 -ion 就成了这一场谈，也指纸上那一节论述。

root: 由动词 discuss 加名词后缀 -ion 构成；源头是拉丁语 discutere（打散、细查）。英语里先指对案件的正式审查，后指多人之间的谈话，现代又用作论文中「讨论」这一章节的名称。

sensesIntro.en: From a room full of voices to a chapter that keeps the voices in order.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一屋子声音，到把这些声音排整齐的一章。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet pushed to the middle of a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满字的纸被推到桌子中间。

branches.en: The first sense is the living talk around the table.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是桌边活生生的谈话。

branches.en: The second sense is the same talk pressed into print.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同一场谈话压进纸里。

branches.en: Both senses hold several views in one place.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把几种看法收在一处。

branches.en: Both can end without a decision.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能没有结论就结束。

branches.en: Only the second sense has a page number.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项带页码。

intro.en: Discussion is the noun built on discuss, inside the small cuss- family from Latin quatere.
intro.cn: discussion 是由 discuss 构成的名词，属于拉丁语 quatere 衍生的 cuss- 小家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin discutere, to shake apart, gives discuss and discussion, with -ion marking the act.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discutere（摇散）给出 discuss 与 discussion，后缀 -ion 标出行为。

items.meaning: the act of talking a subject over

items.exampleCN: 他们每周讨论这个计划。
一位讨论者问到了成本。
这个话题被讨论了很多。
他们正在讨论那张地图。

items.meaning: a striking, as on a drum

definition_en: an illness of the body or mind, or a serious problem in a society
core_image: 一片叶子上出现一块褐色斑点，几天后整枝都软了
scene: 叶面上先出现一个褐色小点，几天后整片叶子都软了。The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
sceneCN: 这里 disease 指「疾病」（第 1 个义项：身体或精神的病症）；句意是那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

senses.title: An illness of the body
senses.definition: an illness that affects the body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 影响身体或精神的病症
senses.example: The disease spread through the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 那种病传遍了果园。
senses.why: A small spot on one leaf is a whole orchard a month later.
senses.whyCN: 一片叶子上的小点，一个月后就是整片果园。

senses.title: A sickness in society
senses.definition: a serious problem that harms a group or a system
senses.definitionCN: 危害群体或制度的严重问题
senses.example: Greed is a disease of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。
senses.why: The same word moves from one body to a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一具身体挪到一群人身上。

intro.en: Disease comes from Old French desaise, a lack of ease, built from des- and aise, comfort.
intro.cn: disease 来自古法语 desaise（不适、不安），由 des-（不）与 aise（安适）构成。

items.en: Adiacens meant lying near, and gave the French word for comfort.
items.cn: adiacens 意为躺卧在旁，后来给出法语里表示安适的词。

items.en: Desaise meant lack of ease or discomfort.
items.cn: 古法语 desaise 指不安适、不舒服。

items.en: English disease first meant unease of any kind.
items.cn: 英语 disease 最初泛指任何不适。

items.en: It narrowed to a named illness of the body.
items.cn: 后来收窄为身体上具体的病症。

items.en: The old sense survives in the idea of a social disease.
items.cn: 旧义在社会弊病这一说法里还留有余影。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on ease, and the meaning group names other words for being unwell.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 ease 构成，近义组列出别的表示身体不适的词。

entries.definition: comfort or freedom from effort
not calm or comfortable
suffering from an illness
the state of being unwell
a feeling of being ill
a small or lasting disorder

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one brown spot and end with a word for a broken system.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个褐色斑点开始，落到一个形容坏制度的词。

normal.en: Dis- plus ease: no ease is disease.
normal.cn: dis 加 ease，失去安适就是病。

normal.en: A garden left alone shows disease first on the oldest leaf.
normal.cn: 无人打理的花园，最老的叶子先显出病。

normal.en: Doctors name a disease so that they can fight one thing.
normal.cn: 医生给病取名，才好集中对付一样东西。

normal.en: A disease of the market hides in plain prices.
normal.cn: 市场的弊病藏在平常的价钱里。

normal.en: Clean water is the cheapest guard against disease.
normal.cn: 干净的水是对抗疾病最便宜的守卫。

abstract.en: Picture one brown spot spreading across a leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一个褐色斑点爬满一片叶子。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held over a sick branch at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一盏灯照着病枝。

abstract.en: Picture a word moving from a body to a whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词从一具身体挪到整座城。

examples.en: The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
examples.cn: 那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

examples.en: Clean water prevents many diseases.
examples.cn: 干净的水能预防许多疾病。

examples.en: Greed is a disease of the market.
examples.cn: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disease 记成「不自在」：dis 是不，ease 是安适，身体不安适就是病；一个群体不安适，就是弊病。

root: 来自古法语 desaise（不适），由否定前缀 des- 与 aise（安适）构成，而 aise 可追到拉丁语 adiacens（躺卧在旁）。英语最初泛指各种不适，十六世纪起收窄为具体的病症，后来又引申指社会的弊病。

sensesIntro.en: From a body that has lost its ease to a system that has lost its health.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一具失去安适的身体，到一个失去健康的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one brown spot on a leaf, and the whole orchard going soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶上一个褐色斑点，整片果园慢慢软下去。

branches.en: The first sense is the illness in a living body.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是活身体里的病症。

branches.en: The second sense carries the illness into a system.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把病带进一个制度。

branches.en: Both senses describe something that spreads by itself.
branches.cn: 两个义项都形容会自己蔓延的东西。

branches.en: Both need a name before they can be fought.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有名字才好对付。

branches.en: Only the second sense is used about money or power.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项会用在金钱或权力上。

intro.en: Disease belongs to the ease family, where comfort, difficulty and illness share one stem.
intro.cn: disease 属于 ease 一族，安适、容易与疾病共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Old French aise, comfort, joins des- to make desaise, and English keeps several relatives of the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 aise（安适）加 des- 成为 desaise，英语保留了同一词干的几个亲属。

items.example: He felt uneasy at the door.
A small unease stayed with her.
The diseased tree was cut down.

definition_en: to change your appearance so that people do not know you, or to hide a feeling or fact
core_image: 镜子里的人贴上一副假胡子，几乎认不出自己
scene: 他对着镜子贴上一副假胡子，连自己都愣了一下。She disguised herself as a nurse to enter the ward.
sceneCN: 这里 disguise 指「伪装」（第 1 个义项：改变外表使人认不出）；句意是她扮成护士进了病房。

senses.title: To change how you look
senses.definition: to change your appearance so that people cannot recognize you
senses.definitionCN: 改变外表让人认不出你
senses.example: She disguised herself as a nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 她扮成护士。
senses.why: A face is a door, and a false beard is a new key.
senses.whyCN: 脸是一扇门，假胡子是一把新钥匙。

senses.title: To hide a feeling or fact
senses.definition: to hide something such as a feeling or a fact
senses.definitionCN: 把情感或事实遮盖起来
senses.example: He could not disguise his anger.
senses.exampleCN: 他掩饰不住怒气。
senses.why: What is covered still shows at the corners of the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 被盖住的东西，仍会从嘴角露出来。

intro.en: Disguise comes from Old French desguisier, where des- reversed a guise, a manner or dress.
intro.cn: disguise 来自古法语 desguisier，前缀 des- 把 guise（样子、装束）反过来。

items.en: Wisa meant manner or way, and reached French as guise.
items.cn: wisa 指方式、样子，进入法语成为 guise。

items.en: Desguisier meant to change the usual manner or dress.
items.cn: 古法语 desguisier 指改变平常的样子或装束。

items.en: English used it for a false dress or appearance.
items.cn: 英语借入后指虚假的装束或外表。

items.en: The noun added the thing worn as a cover.
items.cn: 名词又添上用来遮盖的物件这一义。

items.en: The word now also hides feelings, not only faces.
items.cn: 今天它不只遮脸，也遮情绪。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the guise stem, and the meaning group gathers other ways of covering.
note.cn: 形近组保留 guise 词干，近义组聚起别的遮掩方式。

entries.definition: a way of appearing or behaving
wearing something that hides you
open and not hidden
to cover or hide something
to make something blend into its setting
entries.definitionCN: 使融入环境而不被看见

entries.definition: to keep something from being seen

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a false beard in a mirror and end with a feeling that still shows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从镜前一副假胡子开始，落到一种仍会露出来的情绪。

normal.en: Dis- plus guise: the usual guise is changed.
normal.cn: dis 加 guise，把平常的样子换掉。

normal.en: A guard in an old coat can walk past any gate.
normal.cn: 穿旧大衣的警卫能走过任何一道门。

normal.en: A blessing in disguise hides its good side at first.
normal.cn: 因祸得福的事，起初把好的一面藏起来。

normal.en: A thin smile cannot disguise a tired voice.
normal.cn: 淡淡的笑掩不住疲惫的声音。

normal.en: A fact disguised is still a fact in the room.
normal.cn: 被掩饰的事实，仍留在屋子里。

abstract.en: Picture a false beard stuck on in a mirror.
abstract.cn: 想象对着镜子贴上一副假胡子。

abstract.en: Picture a coat turned inside out.
abstract.cn: 想象一件大衣被翻过来穿。

abstract.en: Picture a smile held a moment too long.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑得稍久了一点。

examples.en: She disguised herself as a nurse to enter the ward.
examples.cn: 她扮成护士进了病房。

examples.en: He could not disguise his disappointment.
examples.cn: 他掩饰不住失望。

examples.en: The delay turned out to be a blessing in disguise.
examples.cn: 这次延误后来倒成了因祸得福。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disguise 记成「换一副样子」：dis 表示改变，guise 是样子，把平常的样子换掉，就是伪装。

root: 来自古法语 desguisier，由 des-（改变、反转）与 guise（样子、装束）构成，guise 又可追到日耳曼语 wisa（方式）。本义是改变平常的装束与举止，后来也从遮脸引申为遮掩情感与事实。

sensesIntro.en: From a face made strange to a feeling that will not stay covered.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张被改得陌生的脸，到一种盖不住的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a false beard pasted on in front of a mirror.
core.cn: 核心意象：镜前贴上一副假胡子。

branches.en: The first sense is the body made unrecognizable.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是身体被改得认不出。

branches.en: The second sense moves the cover inward, onto feeling.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把遮盖挪进心里，盖住情绪。

branches.en: Both senses put something false in front of the true thing.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在真东西前面放一层假的。

branches.en: Both work best when nobody looks twice.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在没人多看第二眼时最管用。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be done with a single smile.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能靠一个微笑完成。

intro.en: Disguise sits in the guise family, where a manner or dress can be put on and taken off.
intro.cn: disguise 属于 guise 一族，样子与装束可以穿上，也可以脱下。

latinIntro.en: Old French guise, a manner, gives English guise and disguise, with des- turning the manner against itself.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 guise（样子）给出英语 guise 与 disguise，前缀 des- 让样子背离自身。

items.example: They disguised the van as a van of flowers.
items.exampleCN: 他们把货车伪装成运花的车。

items.example: He came in the guise of a friend.
A disguised door stood in the wall.
Her undisguised joy filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 她毫不掩饰的喜悦充满房间。

items.meaning: the act of hiding by appearance

items.example: The offer came guised as help.
items.exampleCN: 这个提议以帮助的样子出现。
那场聚会是一场假面舞会。

items.meaning: a cover that blends with the ground

definition_en: a strong feeling of dislike, or to make someone feel this
core_image: 一个人闻到坏掉的食物，脸往后一缩
scene: 他低头闻了闻那碗放了三天的汤，立刻把脸转开。The smell of the bin filled her with disgust.
sceneCN: 这里 disgust 指「厌恶」（第 1 个义项：强烈的反感）；句意是垃圾桶的气味让她满心厌恶。

senses.title: A strong feeling of dislike
senses.definition: a strong feeling of dislike caused by something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 由不快之物引起的强烈反感
senses.example: She turned away in disgust.
senses.exampleCN: 她厌恶地转过身。
senses.why: The body pulls back before the mind finds a word.
senses.whyCN: 身体先退开，脑子才找到词。

senses.title: To cause that feeling
senses.definition: to make someone feel strong dislike
senses.definitionCN: 让人产生强烈反感
senses.example: The mess disgusted everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 那堆脏乱让屋里每个人都反感。
senses.why: A smell can push a whole room toward the door.
senses.whyCN: 一种气味能把整屋子人推向门口。

intro.en: Disgust comes from Old French desgouster, to lose the taste for something, from des- and goust, taste.
intro.cn: disgust 来自古法语 desgouster（失去胃口），由 des- 与 goust（味道）构成。

items.en: Gustus meant taste, and gustare meant to taste.
items.cn: gustus 指味道，gustare 指品尝。

items.en: Desgouster meant to lose the taste for something.
items.cn: 古法语 desgouster 指对某物失去胃口。

items.en: English disgust meant a strong distaste.
items.cn: 英语 disgust 指强烈的反胃感。

items.en: The verb added the sense of causing that distaste.
items.cn: 动词又添上使人产生这种反感的意思。

items.en: It now covers moral repulsion as well as bad food.
items.cn: 今天它既指食物难吃，也指道德上的反感。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on Latin gustus, taste, and the meaning group names stronger forms of dislike.
note.cn: 形近组建在拉丁语 gustus（味道）上，近义组列出更强的反感。

entries.definition: a sudden rush of wind
lively enjoyment in doing something
causing strong dislike
a very strong feeling of disgust
a mild dislike of something
to drive someone away by being unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 因令人不快而使人退开

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bowl gone bad and end with a whole room stepping back.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一碗变质的汤开始，落到整屋子人一起后退。

normal.en: Dis- plus gust: the taste turns against you.
normal.cn: dis 加 gust，味道反过来对付你。

normal.en: Milk left out for a day can disgust a child.
normal.cn: 牛奶在外放一天，能让孩子反胃。

normal.en: A dirty kitchen disgusts more than a loud argument.
normal.cn: 脏厨房比大声争吵更让人反感。

normal.en: Disgusted, he pushed the plate away unseen.
normal.cn: 他一阵反感，悄悄把盘子推开。

normal.en: Some lies disgust people who tell small ones daily.
normal.cn: 有些谎话会让天天说小谎的人也反感。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifted and then set down fast.
abstract.cn: 想象勺子举起又飞快放下。

abstract.en: Picture a face turned toward the window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸转向窗户。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held over the nose and mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手捂住口鼻。

examples.en: The smell of the bin filled her with disgust.
examples.cn: 垃圾桶的气味让她满心厌恶。

examples.en: He looked at the dirty plate in disgust.
examples.cn: 他厌恶地看着那只脏盘子。

examples.en: The state of the kitchen disgusted the inspector.
examples.cn: 厨房的状况让检查员十分反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disgust 记成「坏了胃口」：dis 表示相反，gust 是味道，尝到坏味道就反胃，进而厌恶。

root: 来自古法语 desgouster（失去胃口），由 des-（相反）与 goust（味道）构成，goust 可追到拉丁语 gustus。本义是食物让人反胃，后来从口舌的感觉扩展到对行为与人品的强烈反感。

sensesIntro.en: From a mouth that refuses food to a mind that refuses a deed.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张拒绝食物的嘴，到一颗拒绝某种行为的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face pulled back from a bowl that has gone bad.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸从变质的碗边往后缩。

branches.en: The first sense is the feeling inside the body.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是身体里升起的那种感觉。

branches.en: The second sense is the thing that puts it there.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把它放进身体的那件事。

branches.en: Both senses turn on a loss of appetite.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕胃口的失去。

branches.en: Both begin in the nose before they reach the mind.
branches.cn: 两个义项都先到鼻子，再到心里。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs an object in front of you.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要眼前有个对象。

intro.en: Disgust belongs to the Latin gustus family, where taste and wind share one small stem.
intro.cn: disgust 属于拉丁语 gustus 一族，味道与一阵风共用同一个小词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin gustus, taste, gives goust in French and gust in English, and des- turns taste into its opposite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gustus（味道）在法语里成为 goust，在英语里成为 gust，前缀 des- 把味道翻成反面。

items.meaning: to lose the taste for something

items.example: He was disgusted by the lie.
A disgusting smell rose from the drain.
items.exampleCN: 下水道冒出一股难闻的气味。

items.meaning: relating to the sense of taste

definition_en: a shallow container used for food, or a particular kind of prepared food
core_image: 一只白瓷盘从水里捞起，盘沿还挂着水珠
scene: 水槽里泡着一只白瓷盘，盘沿还挂着水珠。She washed the dishes while the soup cooled.
sceneCN: 这里 dish 指「盘子」（第 1 个义项：盛食物的浅容器）；句意是汤凉着的时候她洗了盘子。

senses.title: A shallow plate
senses.definition: a shallow open container used for serving food
senses.definitionCN: 用来盛食物的浅口容器
senses.example: She put the apples in a glass dish.
senses.exampleCN: 她把苹果放进玻璃盘。
senses.why: A plate is a small stage for food.
senses.whyCN: 盘子是食物的小舞台。

senses.title: A kind of prepared food
senses.definition: a particular food prepared in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式做成的特定食物
senses.example: Fish pie is a local dish.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼派是当地的一道菜。
senses.why: The plate becomes the recipe when a town asks for it by name.
senses.whyCN: 当一座城点得出名字，盘子就成了菜谱。

intro.en: Dish goes back to Latin discus, a flat round object, which also named a plate at table.
intro.cn: dish 可追到拉丁语 discus（扁圆之物），同一个词也指餐桌上的平盘。

items.en: Discus meant a flat round object thrown in games.
items.cn: discus 指游戏中投掷的扁平圆盘。

items.en: The same discus named a flat plate at table.
items.cn: 同一个词也指餐桌上的平盘。

items.en: Disc came into English as a flat dish.
items.cn: disc 进入英语，指平的盘子。

items.en: The spelling softened from disc to dish.
items.cn: 拼写由 disc 软化为 dish。

items.en: Dish then named the food served on it.
items.cn: 后来 dish 也指盛在盘里的菜。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the flat disc shape, and the meaning group names things that hold food.
note.cn: 形近组共享扁圆的盘形，近义组列出别的盛食之物。

entries.definition: a flat round object
a flat round plate or storage medium
the plates used at a meal
a flat dish for one person
a deep round container for food
one part of a meal served at a time

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a plate in the sink and end with a town naming its own food.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从水槽里的一只盘子开始，落到一座城叫得出名字的食物。

normal.en: Dish and disc are cousins: both are flat and round.
normal.cn: dish 与 disc 是亲戚，都扁而圆。

normal.en: One dish, one meal, one hand to carry it.
normal.cn: 一只盘，一餐饭，一只手端它。

normal.en: The dishes pile up faster than the cooking ends.
normal.cn: 盘子堆起来的速度，比做菜结束得快。

normal.en: Every family has one dish that means home.
normal.cn: 每个家庭都有一道菜，等于家。

normal.en: A side dish is small but changes the whole table.
normal.cn: 配菜虽小，却能改变整张桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a white plate lifted dripping from the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只白盘滴着水被捞起来。

abstract.en: Picture a cloth drying the rim in one turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一块布转一圈擦干盘沿。

abstract.en: Picture a name written beside a plate on a menu.
abstract.cn: 想象菜单上一只盘子旁边写着名字。

examples.en: She washed the dishes while the soup cooled.
examples.cn: 汤凉着的时候她洗了盘子。

examples.en: Fish pie is a local dish in this town.
examples.cn: 鱼派是这座城的一道本地菜。

examples.en: He dropped the dish and it broke in two.
examples.cn: 他把盘子掉了，摔成两半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dish 记成「一片平的」：dish 与 disc 同源，都是扁圆的东西；扁圆的是盘子，盘子里的菜也成了 dish。

root: 源自拉丁语 discus（扁圆之物），经古英语 disc 进入英语，本义是扁平圆盘。因为盘子是最常见的扁圆器皿，词形软化为 dish，后来又由「盛在盘里的东西」引申出「一道菜」的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a flat round plate to the food that a town is known for.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一只扁圆的盘子，到一座城因之得名的那道菜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white plate lifted from the water, drops still on the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：白盘从水里捞起，盘沿还挂着水珠。

branches.en: The first sense is the object itself, flat and open.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是器物本身，扁平而敞开。

branches.en: The second sense is what the object is known for holding.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这件器物以盛什么出名。

branches.en: Both senses meet on the same table.
branches.cn: 两个义项在同一张桌上碰头。

branches.en: Both can be counted, washed and broken.
branches.cn: 两个义项都能计数、清洗、摔碎。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be ordered in a restaurant.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能在餐馆里点。

intro.en: Dish belongs to the disc family, where a flat round shape turns into a plate and then into a recipe.
intro.cn: dish 属于 disc 一族，扁圆的形状先变成盘子，再变成菜谱。

latinIntro.en: Latin discus, a flat round object, passes through disc into dish, and the same stem also gives disk.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discus（扁圆之物）经 disc 进入 dish，同一词干也给出 disk。

items.example: The disc lay on the table.

items.meaning: a flat round plate or medium
items.example: Save the file to the disk.

items.meaning: plates and bowls for the table
items.example: The dishware was stacked by the sink.
A wet dishcloth hung on the tap.
items.exampleCN: 一块湿洗碗布挂在龙头上。

items.example: A dishy young actor took the part.
items.exampleCN: 一位英俊的年轻演员接了这角色。

items.meaning: as much as one dish holds
items.example: He ate a dishful of rice.

definition_en: not telling the truth, or intended to deceive people
core_image: 一只手把抽屉关到一半，另一只手还藏在背后
scene: 抽屉被推到一半就停住，另一只手始终没拿出来。It was dishonest of him to keep the money.
sceneCN: 这里 dishonest 指「不诚实的」（第 1 个义项：说话或行事不老实）；句意是他把那笔钱留下是不诚实的。

senses.title: Not telling the truth
senses.definition: saying or doing something that is not true
senses.definitionCN: 说了或做了不真实的事
senses.example: He gave a dishonest answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了一个不老实的回答。
senses.why: A half-closed drawer is its own kind of sentence.
senses.whyCN: 半关的抽屉本身就是一句话。

senses.title: Built to deceive
senses.definition: made or done in order to trick people
senses.definitionCN: 为欺骗别人而做成或做出的
senses.example: The ad used dishonest numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 那则广告用了骗人的数字。
senses.why: A number can lie as easily as a mouth.
senses.whyCN: 数字撒起谎来和嘴一样容易。

intro.en: Dishonest is dis- plus honest, from Latin honestus, honourable, which rests on honos, honour.
intro.cn: dishonest 是 dis- 加 honest；honest 来自拉丁语 honestus（可敬的），其根是 honos（荣誉）。

items.en: Honos meant honour and public respect.
items.cn: honos 指荣誉与公众的敬重。

items.en: Honestus meant honourable and decent.
items.cn: honestus 意为体面的、可敬的。

items.en: Honest entered English as honourable.
items.cn: honest 进入英语时意为可敬的。

items.en: Dis- reversed it into the lacking of honour.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把它翻成缺少荣誉。

items.en: Dishonest now covers lies, tricks and cheating.
items.cn: 今天 dishonest 涵盖说谎、欺骗与作弊。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the honest stem, and the meaning group names other words for a lie.
note.cn: 形近组共享 honest 词干，近义组列出别的说谎之词。

entries.definition: truthful and fair
the quality of being truthful
the practice of telling lies
using lies to get what you want
saying things that are not true
dishonest in business or politics
entries.definitionCN: 生意或政治上的不老实

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a half-shut drawer and end with a trust worn thin.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从半关的抽屉开始，落到一层被磨薄的信任。

normal.en: Dis- plus honest: honour taken away.
normal.cn: dis 加 honest，把可敬拿走。

normal.en: A dishonest shop keeps one bad scale.
normal.cn: 不诚实的店，总会有一杆坏秤。

normal.en: A dishonest answer often arrives too quickly.
normal.cn: 不老实的回答，往往来得太快。

normal.en: One dishonest line can spoil a long report.
normal.cn: 一行不实的话，能毁掉一份长报告。

normal.en: Dishonest money is the most expensive kind.
normal.cn: 不义之财是最贵的一种钱。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer pushed half shut and held.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉被推到一半又停住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand kept behind the back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手始终藏在背后。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that leans by a hair.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤只偏了一点点。

examples.en: It was dishonest of him to keep the money.
examples.cn: 他把那笔钱留下是不诚实的。

examples.en: She refused to sign a dishonest report.
examples.cn: 她拒绝在一份不实的报告上签字。

examples.en: Dishonest traders were banned from the market.
examples.cn: 不诚实的商贩被禁止进入市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dishonest 记成「去掉可敬」：dis 是否定，词根 honest 意为可敬、老实，去掉这一层就是不诚实。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 honest 构成；honest 源自拉丁语 honestus（可敬的），其根 honos 指荣誉与敬重。因此 dishonest 的字面意思是「失去可敬」，英语里用来指说话不实、行事取巧或以骗术待人。

sensesIntro.en: From the plain absence of honour to the habit of bending facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 从荣誉的缺席，到把事实扳弯的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawer pushed half shut, with one hand still behind the back.

branches.en: The second sense is the thing made to trick you.

branches.cn: 两个义项都靠藏起某样东西起作用。

branches.en: Both cost more trust than they gain.
branches.cn: 两个义项花掉的信任都比赚到的多。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be printed in an ad.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能印在广告里。

intro.en: Dishonest is the negative of honest, in the Latin honos family of honour and respect.
intro.cn: dishonest 是 honest 的反面，属于拉丁语 honos（荣誉与敬重）一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin honos gives honestus and then honest, and the prefix dis- removes the honour again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 honos 给出 honestus，再成为 honest，前缀 dis- 又把这份荣誉拿走。

items.example: A dishonest claim was struck out.
items.exampleCN: 一项不实的说法被删去了。

items.example: He spoke honestly about the fault.

items.exampleCN: 不诚实断送了他的职业。

definition_en: in a way that is not truthful, or by cheating
core_image: 一只手把账本上的数字轻轻改小一格
scene: 他把账本上的数字往小改了一格，又把笔放回原处。He dishonestly claimed that the money was lost.
sceneCN: 这里 dishonestly 指「不诚实地」（第 1 个义项：以不老实的方式）；句意是他不诚实地声称那笔钱丢了。

collocations.zh: 以不正当手段取得钱财

senses.title: In an untruthful way
senses.definition: in a way that is not truthful
senses.definitionCN: 以不说真话的方式
senses.example: He answered dishonestly.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答得不老实。
senses.why: A small turn of the pen can move a large sum.
senses.whyCN: 笔尖轻轻一转，能挪动一大笔钱。

senses.title: By cheating or fraud
senses.definition: by cheating or by breaking the rules of fair dealing
senses.definitionCN: 靠欺骗或破坏公平规则
senses.example: The money was obtained dishonestly.
senses.exampleCN: 那笔钱是不正当取得的。
senses.why: What the law calls fraud, the mouth calls a mistake.
senses.whyCN: 法律叫欺诈的事，嘴上叫失误。

intro.en: Dishonestly is dishonest plus -ly, and dishonest is dis- added to Latin honestus, honourable.
intro.cn: dishonestly 是 dishonest 加 -ly；dishonest 则是把 dis- 加在拉丁语 honestus（可敬的）上。

items.en: Honestus meant honourable, from honos, honour.
items.cn: honestus 意为可敬的，其根是 honos（荣誉）。

items.en: Honest first meant honourable in English.
items.cn: honest 在英语里最初意为可敬的。

items.en: The adverb honest-ly named the manner of acting.
items.cn: 副词 honest-ly 用来指行事的方式。

items.en: Dis- turned the manner into its opposite.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把这种方式翻成反面。

items.en: Dishonestly now covers lies in speech and in accounts.
items.cn: 今天 dishonestly 既指言语上的谎，也指账目上的假。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the honest stem, and the meaning group names other manners of cheating.
note.cn: 形近组共享 honest 词干，近义组列出别的欺骗方式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one stroke of a pen and end with a short sum in the book.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笔下的一划开始，落到账上少掉的一笔。

normal.en: Dishonest plus -ly turns the fault into a manner.
normal.cn: dishonest 加 -ly，把毛病变成一种方式。

normal.en: A form filled dishonestly is a lie with boxes.
normal.cn: 不实填写的表格，是带方格的谎。

normal.en: Money gained dishonestly leaves a long shadow.
normal.cn: 不正当得来的钱，留下很长的影子。

normal.en: He dealt dishonestly once and lost ten clients.
normal.cn: 他欺诈过一次，失去了十个客户。

normal.en: A witness who answers dishonestly answers twice.
normal.cn: 证人若不实回答，就得再答一次。

abstract.en: Picture a figure made smaller by one stroke.

abstract.en: Picture a pen set down too carefully.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔被过分小心地放下。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被折进口袋。

examples.en: He dishonestly claimed that the money was lost.
examples.cn: 他不诚实地声称那笔钱丢了。

examples.en: The clerk dealt dishonestly with every customer.
examples.cn: 那名职员对每位顾客都不老实。

examples.en: Goods were obtained dishonestly and returned.
examples.cn: 货物是以不正当手段取得的，已被退回。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dishonestly 记成「不体面地」：dis 是否定，honest 是可敬、老实，-ly 表方式，用不老实的方式做事就是不诚实地。

root: 由 dishonesty 与 -ly 构成，源头是拉丁语 honestus（可敬的）与 honos（荣誉）。字面意思是「以失去可敬的方式」，英语里用来指说话不实或用骗术取利的具体做法。

sensesIntro.en: From the manner of a lying answer to the manner of a false account.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一句不实回答的方式，到一本假账的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in a ledger quietly made smaller by one stroke.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上一个数字被一笔悄悄改小。

branches.en: The first sense is the manner of an untrue answer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是不实回答的那种方式。

branches.en: The second sense is the manner of a cheat or a fraud.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是行骗或欺诈的方式。

branches.en: Both senses describe how an act is done, not what it is.
branches.cn: 两个义项说的都是做法，而不是事情本身。

branches.en: Both need a listener who trusts the speaker.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要一个相信说话人的听者。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be tried in a court.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能在法庭上受审。

intro.en: Dishonestly is the adverb built on honest, inside the Latin honos family.
intro.cn: dishonestly 是由 honest 构成的副词，属于拉丁语 honos 一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin honos, honour, gives honestus, then honest; dis- and -ly turn it into a manner of acting.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 honos（荣誉）给出 honestus，再成为 honest；dis- 与 -ly 把它变成一种行事方式。

items.exampleCN: 这项声明是不实作出的。
一笔不诚实的交易黄了。
不诚实之风蔓延整个办公室。

definition_en: a flat round object, or a device that stores computer data
core_image: 一张银亮的圆片在光下转出一圈亮边
scene: 那台旧机器里，一张银亮的圆片还在慢慢转。The files were saved on a hard disk.
sceneCN: 这里 disk 指「磁盘」（第 2 个义项：计算机的存储盘）；句意是文件存在硬盘上。

senses.title: A flat round object
senses.definition: a flat round shape or object
senses.definitionCN: 扁平圆形的形状或物件
senses.example: A disk of metal lay on the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 工作台上有一个金属圆盘。
senses.why: A coin is a disc that learned to hold value.
senses.whyCN: 硬币就是学会了承载价值的圆片。

senses.title: A store for computer data
senses.definition: a device that keeps computer data on a round magnetic or optical surface
senses.definitionCN: 以圆形磁面或光面保存计算机数据的装置
senses.example: The files are on the hard disk.
senses.exampleCN: 文件在硬盘上。
senses.why: A round plate became a quiet room for memory.
senses.whyCN: 圆盘变成了一间安静的仓库，装着记忆。

intro.en: Disk and disc both come from Latin discus, a flat round object thrown in games and set on tables.
intro.cn: disk 与 disc 同出拉丁语 discus，既指游戏中投掷的扁圆物，也指桌上的平盘。

items.en: Diskos meant a quoit thrown in competition.
items.cn: diskos 指比赛中投掷的铁饼。

items.en: Discus kept both the game piece and the table plate.
items.cn: discus 同时保留游戏器具与餐桌平盘两义。

items.en: English used disc for a round flat thing.
items.cn: 英语用 disc 指圆而扁的东西。

items.en: American spelling disk named the computer medium.
items.cn: 美式拼写 disk 用来指计算机存储介质。

items.en: Disc stays for sound and light, disk for data.
items.cn: 如今 disc 多用于声音与光盘，disk 多用于数据。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the flat round shape, and the meaning group names other round holders.
note.cn: 形近组共享扁圆的形状，近义组列出别的圆形承载物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bright circle and end with a room full of memory.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个亮圆片开始，落到一间装满记忆的屋子。

normal.en: Disk is a flat round thing, like a coin with no face.
normal.cn: disk 是扁圆之物，像一枚没有图案的硬币。

normal.en: A hard disk hides behind a metal box.
normal.cn: 硬盘藏在一只金属盒子后面。

normal.en: A floppy disk bends, and that was its charm.
normal.cn: 软盘能弯，这正是它的可爱处。

normal.en: Disk space runs out exactly when you need it.
normal.cn: 磁盘空间总是在你最需要时用完。

normal.en: The same shape holds music, film and files.
normal.cn: 同一种形状，装着音乐、电影与文件。

abstract.en: Picture a silver circle spinning under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个银圆片在灯下旋转。

abstract.en: Picture a slot swallowing the disk whole.

abstract.en: Picture a small light blinking while data moves.

examples.cn: 文件存在硬盘上。

examples.en: He handed me a disk with the photos.
examples.cn: 他递给我一张存着照片的磁盘。

examples.en: A disk of polished steel covered the hole.
examples.cn: 一块抛光钢圆盘盖住了那个洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disk 记成「扁圆片」：disk 与 dish 同源，都是拉丁语 discus 那种扁圆的东西，电脑把数据也放进了这样的圆片。

root: 源自拉丁语 discus（投掷用的扁圆物），其根可追到希腊语 diskos。英语里 disc 与 disk 原本只是拼写差异，二十世纪以后逐渐分工：disc 多指唱片与光盘，disk 多指计算机的磁盘与硬盘。

sensesIntro.en: From a quoit thrown in a game to a quiet surface that keeps our files.
sensesIntro.cn: 从比赛中投出的铁饼，到安静保存文件的那个面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright metal circle turning under a lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个发亮的金属圆片在灯下转动。

branches.en: The first sense is simply the shape in your hand.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是手里那个形状。

branches.en: The second sense is the shape taught to remember.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这个形状被教会了记忆。

branches.en: Both senses are flat, round and easy to stack.
branches.cn: 两个义项都扁、都圆、都好叠放。

branches.en: Both hide their contents on a surface.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把内容放在一个面上。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs a machine to speak.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要机器才能说话。

intro.en: Disk belongs to the discus family, where a game piece, a plate and a data store share one shape.

latinIntro.en: Greek diskos and Latin discus give disc and disk, two spellings of one flat round idea.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 diskos 与拉丁语 discus 给出 disc 与 disk，同一个扁圆概念的两条拼写。

definition_en: to not like someone or something, or a feeling of not liking
core_image: 一个人把递过来的盘子轻轻推回半寸
scene: 菜被递到他面前，他把盘子轻轻推回了半寸。She dislikes being late more than missing the train.
sceneCN: 这里 dislike 指「不喜欢」（第 1 个义项：对某人某物没有好感）；句意是她讨厌迟到，甚于错过火车。

senses.title: To have no liking for
senses.definition: to feel that someone or something is not pleasant to you
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某人或某事不合自己心意
senses.example: She dislikes being late.
senses.exampleCN: 她不喜欢迟到。
senses.why: A plate pushed back half an inch says everything.
senses.whyCN: 盘子被推回半寸，什么都说了。

senses.title: A feeling of not liking
senses.definition: a feeling that you do not like something
senses.definitionCN: 不喜欢某物的感觉
senses.example: He has a dislike of crowded rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 他讨厌拥挤的房间。
senses.why: The feeling is quieter than hate and longer than anger.
senses.whyCN: 这种感觉比恨安静，比怒持久。

intro.en: Dislike is dis- plus like, from Old English lician, to please, so the word means not to please.
intro.cn: dislike 是 dis- 加 like；like 来自古英语 lician（使人高兴），所以本义是「不使人高兴」。

items.en: Lician meant to please or to be agreeable.
items.cn: lician 指使人愉快、合意。

items.en: Like came to mean to find something pleasant.
items.cn: like 转为主观上的喜欢。

items.en: Dis- was added to reverse the liking.
items.cn: 加上 dis-，把喜欢反转。

items.en: The noun named a settled feeling of distaste.
items.cn: 名词指一种稳定的反感。

items.en: Dislike stays milder than hate in everyday use.
items.cn: 日常用法里，dislike 仍比 hate 温和。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the like stem, and the meaning group names stronger forms of rejection.
note.cn: 形近组共享 like 词干，近义组列出更强的排斥。

entries.definition: to find something pleasant
a feeling of fondness
different from
to feel very strong dislike
to dislike something intensely
to feel angry dislike about something
entries.definitionCN: 对某事怀有反感的恼怒

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a plate pushed back and end with a feeling that stays.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被推回的盘子开始，落到一种留下来的感觉。

normal.en: Dis- plus like: the liking is taken back.
normal.cn: dis 加 like，把喜欢收回去。

normal.en: She dislikes waiting more than walking.
normal.cn: 她讨厌等待，胜于走路。

normal.en: A first dislike can grow from one wrong word.

normal.en: Likes and dislikes are a short map of a person.

normal.en: Disliked dishes are the ones left untouched.
normal.cn: 不讨喜的菜，总是没人动。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth closed before a word forms.
abstract.cn: 想象词还没成形，嘴先闭上。

abstract.en: Picture a chair turned slightly away from the table.
abstract.cn: 想象椅子微微转离桌子。

examples.en: She dislikes being late more than missing the train.
examples.cn: 她讨厌迟到，甚于错过火车。

examples.en: He has a strong dislike of crowded rooms.
examples.cn: 他非常讨厌拥挤的房间。

examples.en: They disliked the plan from the first page.
examples.cn: 他们从第一页起就不喜欢这个计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dislike 记成「不喜欢」：dis 是否定，like 是喜欢，合起来就是把好感收回去。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加动词 like 构成；like 源自中古英语 liken，再往上可追到古英语 lician（使人愉快）。因此 dislike 的字面意思是「不使人愉快」，后来同时用作动词「不喜欢」与名词「反感」。

sensesIntro.en: From the small gesture of refusal to the quiet feeling that stays behind it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个小小的拒绝动作，到留在它背后的那种安静感觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate pushed back half an inch without a word.
core.cn: 核心意象：盘子被推回半寸，没有人说话。

branches.en: The first sense is the act of turning something down.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把东西推开的动作。

branches.en: The second sense is the feeling that remains afterwards.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是动作之后留下的感觉。

branches.en: Both senses work without any loud words.
branches.cn: 两个义项都不需要大声说话。

branches.en: Both can be small enough to hide at a table.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能小到藏在饭桌上。

branches.en: Only the second sense can last for years.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能持续多年。

intro.en: Dislike belongs to the like family, where pleasure, fondness and refusal share one stem.
intro.cn: dislike 属于 like 一族，愉快、喜爱与拒绝共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Old English lician, to please, gives like, and dis- plus -ing build the rest of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 lician（使愉快）给出 like，前缀 dis- 与后缀 -ing 撑起这一族的其余词。

items.example: She has a liking for old maps.

items.example: A dislikeable habit spoiled the talk.
items.exampleCN: 一个招人烦的习惯毁了谈话。

definition_en: to remove someone from a job, or to refuse to consider an idea

collocations.zh: 把某人当成空想家而不予理会

senses.title: To send someone from a job
senses.definition: to remove someone from a job or a position
senses.definitionCN: 使某人失去工作或职位
senses.example: The manager dismissed two workers.
senses.exampleCN: 经理解雇了两名工人。
senses.why: A desk is cleared in minutes, a name in seconds.
senses.whyCN: 桌子几分钟就清空，名字几秒就被划掉。

senses.title: To refuse to consider
senses.definition: to decide that something is not worth thinking about
senses.definitionCN: 认定某事不值得考虑
senses.example: He dismissed the warning as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 他把警告当成玩笑不理。
senses.why: The fastest way to lose an idea is to call it small.
senses.whyCN: 弄丢一个想法最快的办法，是说它太小。

senses.title: To let people leave

senses.why: A wave of the hand can empty a room politely.
senses.whyCN: 一挥手，就能礼貌地清空一间屋子。

intro.en: Dismiss comes from Latin dimittere, to send away, made of dis-, apart, and mittere, to send.
intro.cn: dismiss 来自拉丁语 dimittere（遣散），由 dis-（分开）与 mittere（送）构成。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go.
items.cn: mittere 指送出或放开。

items.en: Dimittere meant to send people away in different directions.
items.cn: dimittere 指把人往各处遣散。

items.en: Desmettre meant to put away or release.
items.cn: 古法语 desmettre 指放走、解除。

items.en: English dismiss meant to send away a crowd.
items.cn: 英语 dismiss 指遣散一群人。

items.en: The sense of removing from a post became common.
items.cn: 免职这一义在十九世纪通行。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dismiss stem, and the meaning group names other ways of pushing someone out.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dismiss 词干，近义组列出别的把人推开的方式。
